Twenty-four comments

Dever the Dancer

I got this tune from fiddler Kevin O’Brien of Boston.

This tune is often paired with “Connie the Soldier,” as flutist John McKenna played it that way on his recordings from the late 1920s.

John Harvey

↳ Posted by Jdharv on June 17th, 2001.

A little Extra

I have taken to playing this tune on top of “Kid on the Mountain” The A parts are amusing together. The B parts are are great together. Just continue with the ’Kid when you are finished with “Dever the Dancer”

Thanks for posting it John
Mark

↳ Posted by Mark Cordova on May 22nd, 2002.

Dever the Dancer

I learned this more than 2 years ago, but haven’t played it for long until it popped out of my flute quite recently. It really goes nicely with Taim in Arrears: https://thesession.org/tunes/993 The two tune actually have similar 2nd parts.

This was submitted by tin_whistler with the title “The Humours of Whiskey”, but no information as to where they’d acquired the tune or the title… Maybe in the future? :-/

↳ Posted by ceolachan on May 10th, 2007.

Well… # Posted on May 10th 2007 by tin_whistler:

“I got the title from Na Piobairi Uilleann’s Volume 1 tutor for the pipes. Which, when I first saw that title, I thought it was already taken by another tune, the version heard from the Chieftains 2 album. Such is Irish music… =) And to think, I was so happy to have finally submitted a tune, better do my homework better next time!! =) I guess the ending is different… For what it’s worth. Oops!” ~ tin_whistler

Dever the Dancer/Mickey Doherty’s

There’s a Donegal variant of this tune on Vincent Campbell’s “The Purple Heather” album. On that album the tune is titled, “Mickey Doherty’s.” There are snaps in the A section, and the endings are different. I’ll post the tune sometime in the future.

Dever The Dancer, X:9

When I play this, it is dancing on the fence between two keys, with both C and C sharp being used. The C# is nonessential, and could be avoided if necessary by lengthening the preceding B note in the 4th measure, or trilling the D note in the 2nd measure of the B part.

↳ Posted by Bryce on April 25th, 2020.

Dever The Dancer, X:10

Correction of the previous ABC entry (#9): B and ^C (C#) are matching in length, and half the length (16th note) of the following D and B notes (8th notes) in both the A and B parts.
